criteria.evidence: Cold-chain freight utility: deep navy type on an ice-blue ground, heavy geometric sans headlines, uppercase mono eyebrows like '01 / YOUR REQUIREMENTS', one dark night-navy route diagram.

Hierarchy is carried by weight and size jumps: the hero headline is far heavier and larger than anything near it, body copy sits at a lighter gray, and the mono eyebrows are the smallest and lightest; the two-tone navy/blue headline would still separate as two gray levels.

'What do you need to ship?' and 'Your route. Our solution.' are consecutive sections using the identical shape - giant left headline with a small right-aligned paragraph - each followed by a grid of bordered white cards.

The hero is a split: eyebrow plus two-tone headline and two buttons on the left, a rounded photograph of a liveried FWL refrigerated truck on the right with a dark caption strip laid over its lower edge.
A real photograph of a Volvo FM reefer carrying the FWL livery anchors the hero, the FWL mark sits in the header and footer, and the clients row uses actual Danone, Шин-Лайн and ХАМЛЕ marks.
The 'Our clients' row shows three full-colour logo images - Danone's blue star figure, the Шин-Лайн red ribbon-and-deer crest, the red ХАМЛЕ wordmark block - not typeset names.
A quote form with From, To, 'Cargo and quantity', Temperature and a date picker, plus three expandable FAQ rows, a language switcher (Русский / Қазақша / English) and a theme toggle.

Genuinely large: the hero and 'What do you need to ship?' headlines run at display scale in a heavy geometric sans. Genuinely small: letterspaced mono micro-labels '— KAZAKHSTAN · CIS · EUROPE', '01 — 06', '02 / OUR PROPOSAL'.
The whole palette is navy, mid-blue and near-white ice; no purple or violet-blue wash anywhere, and the only other hues are the red in the client logos and the blue sky in the truck photo.

No blobs or 3D shapes; the one piece of non-photographic art is a drawn route network - labelled nodes for Europe, Russia, Kazakhstan, CIS countries, Central Asia joined by curved arcs over a dot grid.

The snowflake on the 'Chilled products' and 'Frozen cargo' tiles (and in white on the hero photo caption) is a flat-capped uniform-stroke dendritic glyph that does not match the rounded-cap stroke icon set used for the thermometer beside it - it reads as the ❄ character pressed into service as an icon.

The brighter blue is spent decoratively on headline words ('The right truck for your cargo', 'Our solution.') while every button is the same dark navy as the full-width How-to-book panel and the route map ground, so no colour is reserved for actions.

One continuous near-white ice ground runs the length of the page with a single hairline rule; the tinted and dark grounds belong to specific objects - the quote-form panel, the route map, the How-to-book panel, the carriers panel - not to whole sections.

Besides cards there is the split hero with an overlaid caption strip, a logo row divided by vertical rules, the drawn route network, a bordered accordion list, and a numbered 01/02/03 fleet checklist.

Named clients (Danone, Шин-Лайн, ХАМЛЕ), a real phone number +7 708 180 5200, actual lanes (Within Kazakhstan, Kazakhstan ↔ Russia, Europe ↔ CIS, Russia ↔ Central Asia), and domain-true placeholders 'E.g. dairy products, 12 tonnes' and 'E.g. +2…+6 °C'.
No lorem and no statistics at all - the page makes no '500+ trucks' or '99% on time' claim; the only placeholder-looking text is legitimate form-field placeholder copy.

The last block before the footer turns to a different audience - 'Have a refrigerated truck? Let's work together.' with an 'Offer your truck' button and a three-point list of what to send - rather than repeating the header's 'Find a truck'.
The vertical rhythm is consistently generous and the hero, form panel and carriers panel all hold the same left column, which reads as a decided measure rather than default stacking.

The bespoke route-network diagram and the WhatsApp-native quote flow ('Get a quote on WhatsApp', 'WhatsApp will open with your enquiry') are built for this freight business, not a recoloured stock layout.

Two different cargo categories share one snowflake icon, that icon does not match the icon set beside it, the FAQ's entire left column sits empty below a heading and a phone number, and a single photograph carries a very long page - a studio would fix these before showing it.

defects.what: 'Chilled products' and 'Frozen cargo' carry the identical snowflake icon, so the icon distinguishes nothing between two categories the section exists to distinguish.
defects.where: 'What do you need to ship?' - first and second cards

defects.what: The snowflake is a flat-capped glyph while the thermometer next to it is a rounded-cap stroke icon; two icon languages sit in one row.
defects.where: Cargo-type card icons, and the white snowflake in the hero photo caption strip

defects.what: One photograph in the entire page. Everything below the hero is type, rules and line art, so the page goes visually flat for its whole length - a freight business has trucks, terminals and loading bays to show.
defects.where: Every section from 'Our clients' to the footer

defects.what: The clients row is under-composed: the label sits alone at the far left with a wide void before the first logo, and the three marks are wildly unequal in optical weight (a small blue figure, a fine red crest, a solid red block).
The FAQ's left column holds only a heading and a phone number, leaving a large empty field beside three short accordion rows; the section reads unfinished rather than airy.
Two consecutive sections repeat one header shape - display headline hard left, small right-aligned paragraph - and each is followed by a grid of bordered white cards.
defects.where: 'What do you need to ship?' into 'Your route. Our solution.'

defects.what: Four of the six route cards carry the same link text, 'Discuss this route', so the grid offers no differentiated action and the cards read as one repeated row.
The date field renders the browser's native dd/mm/yyyy control with its own spinner, which does not match the custom-styled text inputs beside it.
defects.where: 'When do you need a truck?' in the quote panel

defects.what: Three of the five quote fields are labelled 'Optional', which tells the visitor most of the form need not be filled and undercuts the form's purpose.
The third cargo card's heading wraps to two lines while the other two stay on one, so its body copy and its link start lower than its neighbours'.
The hero photo caption states the obvious ('FastWay refrigerated trucks / Our fleet and partner vehicles') over an image that already shows exactly that.
defects.where: Caption strip on the hero photograph

defects.what: The theme toggle is an unlabelled icon button sitting immediately beside the primary CTA, competing with it for the eye at the top right.

aesthetic_in_one_phrase: Cold-chain freight utility - navy on ice, heavy geometric sans, mono technical labels and one night-navy route diagram
